summary: This continuation connects the canonical Shimura tower to integral reduction and to a rational conjugacy-quotient class for geometric Frobenius. It imports the normalized interior model, develops its canonical tensors and corrected local geometry, constructs abelian-type descent with conjugated levels, and proves ordinary special lifting and same-residue-field curve comparison. Generic local models, tensor displays and companion theorems remain explicit supplier contracts. Independent Honda–Tate classification, mod-p uniformization, orthogonal cycles and cohomology directions receive separate ownership proposals.

nodes.statement: Fix p>2, a Hodge-type datum (G,X), v|p of E(G,X), and a symplectic embedding with a Z_(p)-lattice Λ. Integral Hodge data consist of a point of the extended building, its full fixer G^fix and connected parahoric G°, a closed lattice realization of the required model, a finite tensor family cutting out that model, and compatible sufficiently small prime-to-p Siegel levels. Comparison through a common neat normal subgroup makes this independent up to canonical equivalence. For a fixed admissible p-level and nested sufficiently small prime-to-p levels K_1^p normal in K_2^p, the transition S_(K_pK_1^p)→S_(K_pK_2^p) is finite étale with the expected finite level action; the pro-object carries a continuous G(A_f^p)-action. On normal components the promoted tensor-compatible level sections are uniquely determined by their generic restrictions.

At x above a point of the Siegel closure, assume the embedding is very good and the corrected tensor-display deformation theorem applies. The completion of the chosen normalization component identifies with the versal (G,μ)-adapted deformation ring R_G. An integral lift belongs to this branch exactly when its p-divisible group with the specified tensors is adapted. The condition uses the integral Frobenius tensors and the G-split Hodge filtration, not only the rational Newton class.

Assume p>2 and a Hodge embedding into a Siegel datum with a self-dual periodic lattice chain L such that G^fix(breve Z_p)=G(breve Q_p)∩GSp(L)(breve Z_p). Take K_p=G^fix(Z_p) and the normalized Hodge closure in that chain-level Siegel model. At every geometric special point x there is a geometric local-model point y for which the strict henselizations, and their completions, are isomorphic. This model is canonical in the PR24 sense and independent of the embedding and lattice within this scope. No global very-good embedding or R-smoothness hypothesis is imposed on the given datum; the modern shtuka comparison imports the corrected very-good auxiliary theory in its proof. The result does not yield a rational local-model point over a prescribed finite residue field.

uses.how: For a geometric special-fibre point x of the normal Hodge model, every characteristic-zero lift through x gives the same rational Frobenius-invariant tensors in D(A_x[p∞])[1/p]^⊗, under the crystalline–de Rham comparisons. This independence holds across the lifts belonging to that normalization point; equality of underlying Siegel points alone does not identify different normalization branches. Integrality is a separate assertion requiring the integral embedding input.

For γ in the positive integral rational adjoint group, let P_γ be its central torsor. Twist the universal abelian object using the imported A6 construction, transport its weak polarization and conjugated prime-to-p level, and use normalization to obtain the integral γ-action. Together with prime-to-p Hecke maps this gives the A_int action; the diagonal rational relation acts trivially. Lift it to the adjoint tensor-frame torsor by quotienting out the central ambiguity of a lift of γ.

For x with abelian fibre A_x over F_p-bar, define I_x as the closed Q-subgroup of (End⁰(A_x))^× preserving the canonical crystalline tensors and all prime-to-p étale tensors; use the rational realization actions after scalar extension, so the functor is imposed on every Q-algebra. Define I_(x/Fq) similarly using End⁰_(Fq)(A_x). The polarization is included with its similitude/Tate line. Integral automorphisms are I_x(Q)∩Aut(A_x), not I_x(Q_p)∩Aut(A_x). This extends the pinned TauCeti abelian endomorphism ring by rationalization and tensor conditions.

For ℓ≠p, refine the ℓ-component of the prime-to-p Shimura tower to obtain its pro-étale K_ℓ-cover, then extend structure group to G(Q_ℓ). On the special fibre this defines a G(Q_ℓ)-local system L_ℓ. At neat level it agrees with the tensor-frame torsor of the abelian H¹ realization; it descends as a local system on the non-neat Shimura stack. A path or frame changes the associated fundamental-group homomorphism only by G(Q_ℓ)-conjugation.

Assume there is an ordinary class [b]_μ∈B(G,{μ_h inverse}), meaning that its dominant Newton point is exactly the Galois average of μ_h inverse. Define the ordinary locus as S_[b]_μ. It is not defined by replacing that equality with the unique maximal acceptable class for an arbitrary inner form. For a strongly acceptable triple the split restriction-of-scalars derived factors provide the required ordinary class.

Let the auxiliary Hodge cover (G_1,X_1) and strongly acceptable target (G_2,X_2) share the adjoint datum and carry symplectic embeddings with characters c_1,c_2. For the strongly acceptable very-special model, pull back the Schubert stratification of the intrinsic local model through the connected adjoint frame diagram. The index set is the dominant inertia-coinvariant coweights λ≤μ_h, with Bruhat closure order and unique extremal index μ_h. The extremal KR stratum is open dense and smooth. nodes.title: Unit eigenvalues in every representation
nodes.statement: For every finite-dimensional algebraic representation θ of G over an algebraic coefficient field of characteristic zero and every special-fibre F_q-point, all Frobenius eigenvalues of θ are units at every finite place away from p. The faithful abelian H¹ realization has algebraic Weil eigenvalues and these are such units; θ occurs as a subquotient of sums of tensor products of that realization and its dual, so the unit property persists. No finite-order determinant hypothesis is imposed on θ itself.

On a comparison curve use companions for semisimple algebraic lisse sheaves on a smooth open curve, allowing a constant twist and finite coefficient extension, and Chebotarev on its dense open. Start with ordinary points, then the top-KR curve meeting the ordinary locus, and descend through the finite KR order. Never extend F_q in this comparison.

sourceIssues.reason: For the natural action on tensor frames, q_loc transports the filtration and is not invariant, whereas the frame projection is invariant. The action map is smooth by composing (g,m)↦(g,gm) with projection; this is exactly the property needed.

sourceIssues.printed: The logarithm argument treats the τ-topologized display coefficient ring as complete for the limiting calculation.
sourceIssues.correction: Prove that the existing ring W-hat(A)[1/p] is already complete and separated for its p-adic topology. Use Zink logarithmic coordinates to prove the shifted tails tend to zero in that topology.
sourceIssues.reason: Convergence in a noncomplete τ-topology does not justify the limit. The correction proves p-adic completeness and uses divisibility plus the logarithmic tail shift to establish the required convergence.

sourceIssues.printed: The gluing formula uses the same connected p-level component for every coset representative j.
sourceIssues.correction: The component associated with j has p-level jK_p°j^(-1). Glue the corresponding conjugated-level connected pieces with the transported actions.
sourceIssues.reason: Changing the p-component of a double-coset representative conjugates its stabilizer. The original identification only works uniformly if those representatives normalize the level.

sourceIssues.printed: Ordinary-class existence is asserted for the inner-form setup without an additional existence hypothesis.
sourceIssues.correction: Define the ordinary locus only after specifying an actual class with Newton point equal to the averaged inverse Hodge cocharacter. Quasi-splitness guarantees existence; general inner forms need not have such a class. Keep the separate local-integrality hypothesis for density.
sourceIssues.reason: For the quaternion division group, transfer to GL₂ over the unramified completion shifts both slopes by one half. Putative ordinary slopes (0,−1) would yield slopes (1/2,−1/2), each once, contradicting the denominator-divisibility constraint for isocrystals. This diagnoses a missing existence premise, not a counterexample to density under local integrality.
